content.user_title: Build PyTorch Models with an ML Specialist
content.value_statement: Machine learning implementation often needs architecture, training, and validation choices aligned together. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a specialist workflow for PyTorch delivery.
actual_capabilities: Guides PyTorch model architecture design with modules, configs, and parameter budgeting.
Plans training loops, checkpointing, validation, and optimizer choices.
Reviews performance options such as torch.compile, gradient checkpointing, and memory reduction.
Defines testing expectations for shapes, gradients, integration, and parameter counts.
Formats implementation plans, progress updates, and final delivery summaries.
Coordinates fixes from ML training debugging outputs.
limitations: The audited package contains guidance prompts, not executable helper scripts or templates.
Generated implementations still need local review, tests, and dependency checks.
Architecture details may require papers, existing code, or user clarification.
Performance estimates depend on hardware, dataset size, and runtime configuration.

use_cases.title: Implement a New Model Architecture
use_cases.description: Turn architecture requirements into a PyTorch implementation plan with modules, configs, tests, and documentation.

use_cases.title: Repair Training Behavior
use_cases.description: Apply targeted fixes to training components after a diagnosis, then define tests that confirm the issue is resolved.

use_cases.title: Prepare Production ML Code
use_cases.description: Review model code for performance, memory use, testing coverage, and delivery readiness before integration.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter Model
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new PyTorch model scaffold.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a PyTorch model for [task]. Include the module structure, config fields, expected inputs, and basic tests.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Training Instability
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate debugging request with an observed failure.
prompt_templates.prompt: My model has [symptom] during training. Review the likely causes, propose a fix, and define validation tests.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Inference Performance
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced optimization request for an existing model.
prompt_templates.prompt: Optimize this PyTorch model for [latency or memory target]. Preserve behavior and include benchmarking guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a Research Architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request based on papers and constraints.
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement the architecture from [paper or notes] with [parameter budget], [hardware limit], and full tests.

output_examples.input: Implement a compact transformer with a 25 million parameter budget.
output: A component plan with embeddings, transformer layers, heads, and estimated parameters.
A testing plan covering shape checks, gradient flow, parameter count, and integration behavior.
A delivery summary listing model files, validation status, and performance notes.

output_examples.input: The adaptive computation head always reports zero variance.
output: A diagnosis-focused implementation plan for the loss calculation and calibration behavior.
A test strategy that checks nonzero variance and verifies training continues without warnings.
A concise explanation of the changed training objective and expected tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Reduce inference time without increasing memory use.
output: A prioritized optimization checklist for compilation, batching, caching, and tensor operations.
Benchmark guidance comparing baseline and optimized latency under the same hardware settings.
Risk notes for numerical stability and behavior preservation.

best_practices: Provide architecture constraints, hardware limits, and expected inputs before requesting implementation.
Ask for tests that cover shapes, gradients, integration, and parameter counts.
Review generated changes locally before training on real data or deploying the model.
anti_patterns: Do not request large architecture changes without a parameter budget or target hardware.
Do not accept performance claims without reproducible benchmark settings.
Do not skip tests for gradient flow, checkpoint loading, and train or eval mode behavior.

faq.question: What frameworks does this skill focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on PyTorch model implementation, training loops, optimization, and testing practices.

faq.question: Can it implement models from research papers?
faq.answer: Yes, when you provide enough architecture details, constraints, and expected behavior.

faq.question: Does the package include executable templates?
faq.answer: No. The audited package contains the skill instructions and specialist prompt only.

faq.question: Can it debug failed training runs?
faq.answer: It can implement fixes from a diagnosis and define tests that confirm the fix.

faq.question: Does it guarantee production readiness?
faq.answer: No. You still need local review, dependency checks, tests, and deployment validation.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
